text: ← Advanced contents AVAILABLE CHAPTERS WHAT YOU WILL LEARNExpress a homogeneous ellipsoid’s interior gravity through three coefficients and check axis ratios, positions and the spherical limit. Connect to foundations: The virial theorem: why shrinking stars heat up ↗ Compare solution assumptions and boundary data in the solution library ↗ 01Let the shape depart from a sphere Consider a homogeneous Newtonian ellipsoid with semiaxes a, b and c. It isolates the effect of shape rather than modelling a realistic star or galaxy. Interior points satisfy x²/a²+y²/b²+z²/c² ≤ 1. M = 4π3ρabc, Φ = Φ₀+πGρ(A₁x²+A₂y²+A₃z²) A quadratic interior potential gives forces linear in coordinates. This expression does not describe the exterior. The constant Φ₀ uses the convention that potential vanishes at infinity. 02Define three coefficients by quadrature Δ(u) ≡ √[(a²+u)(b²+u)(c²+u)] Aᵢ = abc∫0∞du(aᵢ²+u)Δ(u), Φ₀ = −πGρabc∫0∞duΔ(u) Use the integral representation as the supplied solution obtained from Newtonian potential theory. u has units of length squared; the Aᵢ are dimensionless and depend only on axis ratios. A common rescaling of all axes leaves them unchanged. gᵢ = −∂Φ∂xᵢ = −2πGρAᵢxᵢ The panel maps the infinite integration interval to a finite one. It computes each coefficient independently and checks the sum below rather than enforcing it by renormalization. 03Check Poisson’s equation Differentiate 1/Δ to obtain −(1/2Δ)Σ1/(aᵢ²+u). Its integral fixes the coefficient sum from endpoint values. Inserting it into the interior Laplacian checks Poisson’s equation. A₁+A₂+A₃ = −2abc[1Δ(u)]0∞ = 2 ∇²Φ = 2πGρΣAᵢ = 4πGρ The panel fixes abc = 1, comparing shapes at fixed mass and density. Flattening can increase A₃ while shortening c, so surface acceleration depends on both the coefficient and position. 04Binding energy and the spherical limit W = −3GM²10∫0∞duΔ(u) a=b=c=R : Aᵢ=23, W=−3GM²5R W includes the factor of one half preventing double counting of pair energy. −W/(GM²) has inverse-length units. The panel fixes the equal-volume radius to one; its displayed energy factor is not in joules. The spherical limit and permutations of the axes give independent checks. Verify the sum of two and each spherical value of two thirds before examining elongated shapes. 05Add rotation and pressure A prescribed homogeneous shape need not be an equilibrium. Pressure and rotation must support an equipotential boundary. The tensor-virial chapter constructs this additional condition. The plot recomputes the homogeneous-ellipsoid integrals, not observations or N-body figures. A collisionless stellar system also needs a velocity-dispersion tensor and an orbital distribution. CHECK YOUR UNDERSTANDING Pause and work it out. For a = b = c = R, what are the three A coefficients and the interior gravitational field? Show the answer and reasoning Symmetry and the sum rule give Aᵢ = 2/3. Thus gᵢ = −(4π/3)Gρxᵢ: interior gravity grows linearly with distance. This differs from the exterior inverse-square field. REFERENCES & PHYSICAL INPUTS Explanations and derivations are written for this guide. References may use different notation or normalization. Panel methods and approximations are stated in the text.
